section: Growth of communal politics - separate electorates, Two-Nation theory, Lahore Resolution 1940

accepted.s: What was the principal historical significance of the system of separate electorates in British India?
o: It introduced provincial autonomy and abolished the Muslim League
It created a single national electorate based on linguistic representation
It established universal adult franchise and ended communal politics
It institutionalised religion in political representation and contributed to the growth of the Two-Nation Theory and Partition
accepted.x: Separate electorates institutionalised religion as the basis of political representation. This strengthened communal politics and became a seed of the Two-Nation Theory and the eventual Partition.
accepted.tq: Identify the cause-and-effect chain linking an institutional arrangement with its wider historical consequences.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding interpretations of the Partition of India:

List-I (View)
 a. Imperialist view
 b. Nationalist view
 c. Marxist view

List-II (Interpretation)
 i. Partition resulted from an elite deal
 ii. Partition was inevitable
 iii. Partition was encouraged by divide and rule and the Muslim League's intransigence

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: a–ii, b–iii, c–i
a–iii, b–i, c–ii
a–i, b–ii, c–iii
a–ii, b–i, c–iii
accepted.x: The imperialist interpretation regards Partition as inevitable; the nationalist interpretation emphasises divide and rule and League intransigence; the Marxist interpretation views it as an elite deal.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes that reverse the three interpretations.

accepted.s: The Hindu op-ed titled “The insidious return of separate electorates”, published on 11 May 2026, revisited which historical feature?
o: The communal basis of the provincial elections held in 1946
The election of the Constituent Assembly through universal adult franchise
The introduction of dyarchy in the provincial elections of 1919
The replacement of provincial elections by nominations in 1946
accepted.x: The op-ed revisited the fact that the 1946 provincial elections were conducted along communal lines, raising the contemporary concern of a return of separate-electorate politics.
accepted.tq: Link a current-affairs reference with the precise historical issue it discusses.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding the Dravidian political response to the demand for Pakistan?
o: Erode Conference, 1938 — Dravida Nadu was demanded in reply to Jinnah's Pakistan demand
Salem Conference, 1940 — Dravida Nadu was demanded in reply to Jinnah's Pakistan demand
Salem Conference, 1938 — Periyar demanded Dravidistan in reply to Jinnah's Pakistan demand
Erode Conference, 1940 — Periyar demanded Dravidistan in reply to Jinnah's Pakistan demand
accepted.x: At the Erode Conference in 1940, Periyar demanded Dravidistan in response to Jinnah's demand for Pakistan.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the similar conference names, years and political demands.

accepted.s: The Salem Conference of 1938 is associated with which of the following demands?
o: Abolition of separate electorates
Pakistan
Dravidistan
Dravida Nadu
accepted.x: The Salem Conference of 1938 sought Dravida Nadu. The demand for Dravidistan was made by Periyar at the Erode Conference in 1940 in response to Jinnah's Pakistan demand.
accepted.tq: Use the conference–demand association rather than confusing it with the later Erode Conference demand.
